problem_statement: The technext Robot Factory site is a static Bootstrap product-landing site for a robotics manufacturer: a dark charcoal design system with a shared navbar (brand logo, a products cart badge, and Home / About / Shop / FAQ / Contact links), a robot hero, a three-item product teaser, a history section, a partners strip, a footer, and a dedicated Shop page (shop.html) with a grid of product boxes. There is no build step; the site is served as static HTML. What the catalog still lacks is its own interactive browse surface: a shopper cannot filter the production robots by line, and the shared navbar links Shop but nothing that lets a visitor browse the fleet by category from anywhere. Add a shared 'Robot catalog' browser (class robot-catalog): an eyebrow 'Browse the fleet', a title 'Robot catalog', a line category tab bar (class cat-tabs) with All lines / Assembly / Logistics / Inspection, a #cat-readout that reflects the selected line, and a grid (class cat-grid) of product cards (class cat-card, each a product image, an <h3> name, a model token, a line chip, and a blurb) that appears IDENTICALLY on BOTH the home page and the Shop page so a visitor browses the same catalog wherever they are. Wire the tabs so clicking a line filters the visible cards and updates #cat-readout live (reflecting the tab actually clicked, not a stale captured value), register a 'Catalog' nav-link in the shared nav registry (js/nav-links.js) so the a.nav-link renders cross-page, and keep the tab bar and card grid from overflowing at 390px. Preserve the existing landing page, navbar, cart badge, hero, product teaser, history, partners, footer, Shop page product boxes, local assets, and static serving behaviour, and keep the page free of remote assets and runtime errors.
required_content: Add a shared 'Robot catalog' section (class robot-catalog) rendered identically on BOTH the home page (index.html) and the Shop page (shop.html): an eyebrow 'Browse the fleet', a title 'Robot catalog', a line category tab bar (class cat-tabs) with an 'All lines', 'Assembly', 'Logistics', and 'Inspection' button (class cat-tab), a #cat-readout that starts at 'Showing all 8 robots', and a grid (class cat-grid) of eight product cards (class cat-card), each with a local product image, an <h3> name, a model token, and a line chip.

Wire the category tabs so clicking the 'Logistics' tab filters the visible product cards to the logistics robots and updates #cat-readout live to 'Showing 3 · Logistics' (and the 'All lines' tab back to 'Showing all 8 robots'); the readout and the visible cards must reflect the tab that was actually clicked, not a stale captured value.

Render the eight production robots — Weld-Arm A5, Torque-Bot T2, Fit-Press F9, Haul-Mule H7, Sort-Runner S3, Lift-Deck L4, Scan-Eye E1, and Gauge-Pod G6 — each as a shared product card with an <h3> name, a local product image, a model token, and its line, on both pages.
Register the Catalog entry in the shared nav registry (js/nav-links.js) so an a.nav-link with text Catalog renders cross-page on both the home page and shop.html.

Preserve original visible content including the Robot Factory brand, the 0 products cart badge, Home/About/Shop/FAQ/Contact nav entries, the Save time and lower hero, the Robot Factory product teaser, the Discover Our History section, the Partners strip, and the footer.
Preserve local static assets including index.html, shop.html, assets/css/main.css, assets/js/script.js, and the product images under assets/images/, and make no remote/CDN request.
design_constraints: Keep the static HTML/CSS/JS implementation; do not add a framework, build step, package dependency, server router, or remote asset.

The Robot catalog must reuse the site palette (dark #262626 ground, white/gray text, orange #f26522 accent) and compact rounded card treatment; the product cards must stay legible (readable name/token/blurb text on the dark ground) and must not collapse into an unreadable dark-on-dark or overlapping card layout.
The Robot catalog must appear on BOTH pages with the same markup and chrome; a catalog that only appears on the home page breaks the cross-page browse invariant.
The tab bar and product-card grid must wrap on a 390px phone; a fixed-width non-wrapping row (masked with overflow-x:hidden) still overflows the document and is not a fix.
The category tabs must re-read the clicked tab on each click and re-filter the visible cards; a handler that only moves the active class but leaves #cat-readout and the cards stale is not acceptable.
Register the Catalog entry once in the shared nav registry so the same a.nav-link appears on every page; do not hand-duplicate a bespoke nav per page.
Desktop, tablet, and 390px mobile states must not introduce horizontal overflow or emit console/network errors.

change_completion: The shared Robot catalog renders on BOTH the home page and the Shop page with the eyebrow, title, line tab bar, #cat-readout, and the eight product cards.
The Catalog nav-link is registered in the shared nav registry and renders cross-page, and the product cards render from the shared card chrome on both pages.
design_consistency: The Robot catalog matches the dark charcoal palette, orange accent, shared card treatment, and container rhythm on both pages, with legible readable product cards.
The original hero, product teaser, history, partners, footer, and mobile navigation remain visually intact.
regression: Original navbar labels, cart badge, hero copy, history heading, partners, footer labels, the mobile navbar toggler behaviour, and local product images remain present.
No new dependency, framework, remote asset, or route system is introduced.
responsive: Desktop, tablet, mobile home, the mobile Robot catalog, and the Shop page have no horizontal overflow.
The Robot catalog tab bar and product-card grid wrap cleanly on 390px mobile.

state_constraints: desktop_home, mobile_home, and tablet_home verify the home page renders the shared navbar with the registered Catalog nav-link cross-page, the shared Robot catalog, and the original hero/teaser/history/partners/footer intact.
desktop_home_catalog and mobile_home_catalog verify the Robot catalog renders on the home page on-palette with legible product cards and a wrapping tab bar / card grid.
desktop_shop and mobile_shop verify the Shop page renders the shared Robot catalog (product names, images, tokens) with the shared navbar and footer.
desktop_shop_catalog verifies the SAME shared Robot catalog renders on the Shop page (cross-page invariant).
desktop_filter_logistics verifies that clicking the 'Logistics' line tab filters the visible cards and updates #cat-readout to 'Showing 3 · Logistics'.
tablet_shop verifies the Shop page holds up at the tablet viewport without overflow.
scoring_notes: L4: the bad leg fails four orthogonal gates — D6 no_horizontal_overflow (masked mobile overflow on the product-card track), D3 visual_regression (product cards broken: dark-on-dark unreadable text + overlapping cards), D2 dom_assertions (Catalog nav-link unregistered cross-page), and D4 interaction_assertions (line tab moves active but leaves #cat-readout stale and never filters the cards). Baseline fails D6 + D3 + D2 (unregistered nav + fixed-nowrap overflow + cramped single-row layout) as the original omission but passes D4 because its filter JS is correct.
